sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Sales of Musical Instruments and Studio Audio Gear

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (with strong EU legal integration)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) – China Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force)
Luxembourg – China Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement signed 1994, as amended by Protocol of 2013 (in force)
OECD Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (in force)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended (notably articles 13-1 et seq. for the SCSp); Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners, as amended; Law of 19 December 2002 on the commercial and companies register and on the annual accounts of undertakings, as amended; implementing Grand-Ducal regulations and CSSF AML/CFT guidance.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Constituting deed of the SCSp / partnership agreement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary (notaire) or foreign notary if executed abroad
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Luxembourg notarial protocol; if executed abroad, Hague Apostille or consular legalization by the competent authority of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity card of each general partner and every beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent government authority of the partner's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions, consular legalization by the Luxembourg embassy or consulate of that country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and current corporate extracts for a corporate limited partner or general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate register of the entity's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions, consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing and corporate authorization / board resolution for corporate founders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home jurisdiction companies registry and corporate secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions, consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners holding at least 25% of capital or voting rights, commercial agents, and legal representatives against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, and Luxembourg national designations under the 2004 AML/CFT Law, as amended. PEP status must be assessed in accordance with FATF Recommendation 12 and the Luxembourg AML/CFT Law; enhanced due diligence is required for PEPs, high-risk third countries, or where source-of-wealth documentation is incomplete. Beneficial ownership must be pierced through trusts, foundations, and intermediary entities before formation. This non-regulated retail musical-instruments e-commerce activity is categorized as low risk but remains subject to Luxembourg AML/CFT filing and record-keeping duties.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – online RCS portal (https://www.lbr.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed using Latin alphabetic characters. A name originating in a non-Latin script must be transliterated into French, German, or Luxembourgish and accompanied by a certified translation. Statutory RCS filings are made in French, and the SCSp name must contain the suffix 'SCSp' or the full term 'société en commandite spéciale'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservations made through LBR/RCS are valid for 30 calendar days and are not routinely renewable; upon expiry, a new reservation application must be filed. If the RCS registrar rejects a name, the applicant may request written grounds, amend the name and resubmit, or file a formal reconsideration request with LBR. If the rejection is upheld, an administrative appeal may be brought before the Minister of the Economy within one month of notification. Judicial annulment proceedings may be initiated before the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg within three months of the refusal decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Domiciliation and virtual office arrangements are permissible for a non-regulated e-commerce retail activity, provided the SCSp maintains a valid Luxembourg registered street address supplied by an authorized domiciliation agent. A P.O. box alone is not sufficient. Virtual office services do not by themselves create tax substance; the SCSp should maintain appropriate accounting, banking, and AML/CFT records in Luxembourg.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for a non-regulated online musical instruments and audio gear retailer; estimated annualized risk of unannounced on-site inspection is below 5%, subject to exceptions triggered by RBE inconsistencies, tax reporting anomalies, or a confidential report to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF/FIU).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-page certified translator tariff; prevailing market benchmark EUR 150–400 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market package for registered office and statutory correspondence handling; EUR 900–1,200

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 34-48 (Société en Commandite Simple rules) and Articles 49-50 (Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp)), as introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013; supplemented by the amended Law of 19 December 2008 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) and the amended Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) division, Luxembourg, served through the eJustice / MyGuichet one-stop-shop electronic portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte de société (partnership agreement / deed of constitution) filed together with the electronic RCS A-Form (formulaire A) via the eJustice platform; statutory publication is effected in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital, no bank escrow / blocking account and no statutory capital account rules apply to an SCSp under the amended Law of 10 August 1915 (Articles 49-50); contributions and future capital calls, if any, are freely fixed in the partnership agreement and evidenced by contractual capital accounts rather than subscribed share capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At the constitutive meeting of the partners of [SCSp Name] (the Partnership), the resolutions below were duly adopted. (1) Subscription: the Initial Partner subscribes to its partnership interests as stated in the executed partnership agreement, with capital, profit and loss accounts accordingly. (2) Registered Office: the Partnership's registered office is fixed at 8, rue Goethe, L-1637 Luxembourg, until amended by partner resolution. (3) Management: [Name] is appointed Gérant with full authority to bind the Partnership, open bank accounts, execute contracts, and represent it before the RCS and tax authorities. (4) Filing: counsel is authorized to file the deed, effect publication, and submit the beneficial-owner declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name verification and professional domiciliation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — public RCS search database (www.lbr.lu); approved Luxembourg domiciliation agents.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an LBR full-text search for the intended SCSp name to verify that no identical or confusingly similar name is already registered; simultaneously engage a licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent and secure a compliant professional registered address for the SCSp. Obtain the domiciliation letter and the agent's acceptance before proceeding to deed drafting.
required_dossiers: Draft partnership agreement synopsis
Passport or national ID of the general partner (associé commandité)
Proof of residential/professional address of the initial partner
Signed domiciliation letter from the approved domiciliation agent
AML/KYC questionnaire of the intended SCSp
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search flags an identical/conflicting entity, submit two ranked alternative names and rerun the search on the same day; if the domiciliation agent rejects the KYC file, supplement the missing documents within 5 business days or retract to a backup approved agent, preserving the RCS filing deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the SCSp partnership agreement (acte de société)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (for real-property contributions) or authorized formation counsel with eJustice filing credentials (for cash/movable contributions).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and execute the partnership agreement in compliance with Articles 49-50 of the amended Law of 10 August 1915. Include the mandatory particulars: partners' identities, firm name and purpose, registered office address, contribution schedule or call provisions, profit/loss apportionment, duration of the partnership, and the Gérant's management and representation powers. If assets physically located in Luxembourg include real estate, execute by authentic notarial deed; otherwise execute under private signature and have the signatories' signatures duly certified or legalized as required by the RCS.
required_dossiers: Final signed partnership agreement (acte de société)
Apostilled or legalized KYC documentation of all partners
Consent to Gérant appointment signed by each partner
AML/KYC source-of-funds declaration for cash contributions
Power of attorney of formation counsel, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries missing or defective clauses in the deed, prepare a corrective supplementary deed (acte modificatif) curing the particulars and resubmit via eJustice within 5 business days of the query; correction before formal refusal avoids costs and preserves the original filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration through eJustice and RESA statutory publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) filing department via eJustice / MyGuichet.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining a filer token, open a new RCS file, select 'constitution' (new legal person), upload the scanned acte de société together with the duly completed electronic RCS Form A and the Gérant's specimen signature card, and pay the EUR 75+ registration/publication duties online. The RCS verifies against the 1915 Law, allocates the RCS file number, and automatically publishes the required particulars in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA); retain the RESA extract as proof of third-party effectiveness.
required_dossiers: Executed acte de société in electronic copy
Completed RCS electronic Form A (identification sheet)
List of managers (Gérant) with specimen signatures
Domiciliation letter from the domiciliation agent
Proof of online payment of the registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a réquisition (query), cure the stated defects and refile within one month; an express refusal may be appealed within two months before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber) in accordance with the amended Law of 19 December 2008. While the appeal is pending, request a provisional negative certificate if urgent banking onboarding requires evidence of filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial owner registration in the RBE
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) unit, under the authority of the Ministry of Justice.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of the RCS registration, submit the RBE declaration under the amended Law of 13 January 2019, identifying each natural person who directly or indirectly holds more than 25% of the SCSp's capital, voting rights or control. Complete the electronic RBE form via the eJustice token, attaching the ID copies and title documents; update the register without delay upon any subsequent change in beneficial ownership. Access to the registered data is governed by the 2019 Law and GDPR.
required_dossiers: RBE electronic form for each beneficial owner
Passport or national ID copy of each beneficial owner
RCS extract confirming the file number
Pages of the partnership agreement evidencing percentage entitlements
Proof of address of the filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE unit returns the declaration for incomplete title evidence, file a corrected declaration within 10 days to avoid the late-filing fine mechanism; in case of a false-positive duplicate record, file a formal request for rectification with the RBE unit supported by the RCS extract.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT / EORI registration and social security employer file opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) — Bureau d'imposition; EU customs Union EORI allocation by the Customs and Excise Administration (ADA); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for Luxembourg VAT using the AED VAT form for business commencement, as online retail supplies of musical instruments from a Luxembourg fixed establishment are taxable in Luxembourg; simultaneously obtain an EORI number for intra-EU and third-country import/export of audio gear. If the SCSp employs staff, open an employer file with the CCSS and enrol personnel with the CNS within eight days of the first hire. Electronically subscribe via Guichet.lu using the business eDelivery token.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate of incorporation (extract)
RBE registration receipt
VAT registration form (formulaire TVA 0101) with expected turnover declaration
EORI application with customs authorization
IBAN proof in the SCSp name
Employer's identity and criminal record extract of the Gérant (if employees are hired)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AED queries the place-of-taxation analysis for distance sales, provide a concise place-of-supply memorandum under Articles 58 and 59 of the VAT Code and Directive 2006/112/EC as amended; late VAT registration may be regularized by a spontaneous declaration before the administration imposes late-filing penalties. For EORI rejections caused by an incomplete address, correct the RCS address first and resubmit immediately.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie — Direction générale des Classes Moyennes (General Directorate for SMEs, Trades and Commerce), acting through the Guichet.lu / MyGuichet establishment permit application portal.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Establishment Permit) issued under the amended Law of 2 September 2011 regulating access to the trades of merchant, artisan, industrialist and certain liberal professions; online retail of musical instruments and studio audio gear qualifies as a commercial (merchant) activity and requires this permit before the commencement of operations, notwithstanding the absence of any sector-specific statutory license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement — Directorate for Waste and Circular Economy (Luxembourg Environment Agency, Ministry of Environment, Climate and Biodiversity).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category C retail/warehouse activity not listed in Annex I or II of the amended Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment; no EIA screening or registration required for a pure online sales warehouse without manufacturing or surface finishing.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or combustion discharges at a retail storage site; municipal sewer compliance applies. Hazardous e-waste (returned amplifiers, mixers and battery-operated gear) must be handled under EU WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU as transposed by Luxembourg circular-economy legislation; packaging put on the market triggers the reporting and recovery duties of the EU Packaging Directive 94/62/EC as amended; volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions are below the 0.5 t/yr exemption threshold of the EU Solvent Emissions Directive 1999/13/EC, hence no solvent management plan is due.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Communal fire-safety inspection for the storage and dispatch area, culminating in the fire-safety certificate (certificat de sécurité incendie) issued by the municipal authority with the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours; occupational clearance by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) based on a workplace risk assessment and general protection statement under the Luxembourg Labour Code; in the absence of mezzanine racking or machinery, no structural load inspection is triggered, but any high-level shelf systems must respect the manufacturer's load ratings and the ITM storage-safety guidance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) — direct taxes; Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) — VAT and registration; consolidated e-portals: MyGuichet.lu, impotsdirects.public.lu, lbr.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident-owned SCSp must (1) execute the partnership deed (private deed suffices unless real property is contributed) and appoint an EU/Luxembourg-resident general partner; (2) register with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) within one month, obtaining the RCS number; (3) publish the formation notice in the RESA electronic compendium; (4) file electronic form 645 / N°TVA registration on MyGuichet addressed to the AEDT, attaching the RCS extract, deed and IBAN; (5) obtain the Luxembourg national identification number (NIN) and a 'LU' VAT identification number issued by the AEDT; (6) designate a local VAT representative where the general partner and all partners are non-EU residents. No minimum capital is required; the SCSp is not subject to corporate income tax or municipal business tax owing to statutory fiscal transparency.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Fiscal transparency is statutory, not elective; no check-the-box election exists in Luxembourg. Available elections: (a) VAT fiscal unity (assujetti unique) under Art. 61 of the VAT Law; (b) small-business franchise election below EUR 25,000 VAT-exclusive turnover; (c) where the sole managing partner is an S.à r.l./S.A., corporate income tax and municipal business tax apply at that partner level. The ATAD reverse-hybrid rule (Law of 31 March 2017) may recharacterise the SCSp as taxable if all investors are non-EU residents and treat the vehicle as opaque in their own jurisdictions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA) under the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 25,000 annual VAT-exclusive turnover for the small-business franchise exemption; compulsory registration from the first euro where a Luxembourg establishment is used; for distance sales of musical instruments and audio gear to EU consumers, the EUR 10,000 Union-wide threshold triggers OSS registration and destination-state VAT liability.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time clearance or digital-stamping mechanism exists; there is no transactional fiscal API approval. B2G electronic invoicing via PEPPOL BIS 3.0 / EN 16931 is mandatory since 1 January 2021; B2B e-invoices are legally accepted with recipient consent; VAT returns and e-CDF/e-FDF archiving are filed electronically through MyGuichet. Mandatory structured e-invoicing under the EU ViDA initiative is pending and not yet transposed.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated under Art. 61(1) of the VAT Law when goods are dispatched or transported outside the EU by the seller or for the account of a non-EU customer and leave EU territory within 90 days of the supply; offshore services (software downloads, remote technical support, e-commerce fulfilment) to non-EU business customers are zero-rated under place-of-supply rules; intra-EU consumer distance sales remain taxable in the destination member state and are reported through OSS rather than as Luxembourg exports.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (EX-A) lodged via Luxembourg Customs' electronic AES/EOS platform, classifying goods under applicable HS codes (e.g. 9206/9207-8471/8518 for musical instruments and audio equipment)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR consignment note evidencing physical departure of the goods from EU customs territory
Commercial invoice and sales contract matching the declared customs value and identifying the non-EU buyer (Incoterms 2020)
Official proof-of-exit evidence: customs stamp, T1/transit discharge, or carrier exit confirmation from the shared EU customs systems (ICS/AES)
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 settlement record evidencing foreign-currency payment into the SCSp's bank account
Carrier track-and-trace logs and Stripe/PayPal platform settlement reports retained for at least six years
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT applies a standard 3-year assessment window, extended to 5 years (10 in cases of fraud) for export exemptions; missing or fabricated exit evidence triggers retroactive VAT reassessment at 17% plus statutory late-payment interest. Fines under Art. 65 VAT Law range from EUR 750 to EUR 12,500 per incident; fraudulent zero-rating claims are punishable under Art. 67 VAT Law with fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years, joint and several liability of the general partner, VAT-number suspension or deregistration, and inclusion in cross-border mutual-assistance exchange.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), as the national central bank within the Eurosystem, with banking supervision jointly exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF); monetary policy is set by the European Central Bank (ECB).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg provides full and unrestricted currency convertibility on both the current and capital accounts under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) and the Eurosystem legal framework. No exchange controls, foreign-currency account licensing, or profit-remittance restrictions exist for a fiscally transparent SCSp; distributions to partners are not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax. Practical remittance frictions are limited to AML/CFT source-of-funds verification, CRS/FATCA reporting, ATAD substance documentation, and EU/UN sanctions screening applicable to the receiving jurisdiction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, mandatory conversion, or holding-time requirements apply to export receipts in Luxembourg; exporters may freely retain and deploy EUR or any foreign currency. The sole regulatory overlay is the BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting regime, executed by resident credit institutions on behalf of the BCL, with direct enterprise reporting required where an individual cross-border payment exceeds the applicable statistical threshold.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Dual capital-escrow and operational EUR account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational account with SEPA credit transfer and instant-credit rails
Operational account with commercial trade-finance and LC module
Operational account with FX hedging and multicurrency capability
Operational account with e-commerce settlement reconciliation

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium-High as a secondary settlement rail for Stripe/PayPal sweeps; Low as the sole primary treasury institution. Legal constraints: under PSD2 and the Luxembourg Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services, only a Luxembourg-licensed or EEA-passported payment/e-money institution (EMI) may legally open an e-money account for the SCSp; an offshore (non-EEA) EMI cannot hold client funds unless it obtains a Luxembourg branch licence or an EEA passport. EMI balances are safeguarded in segregated accounts but are not covered by the Luxembourg Deposit Guarantee Scheme, and EMIs impose full RBE/UBO disclosure and source-of-funds files equivalent to credit-institution standards for pass-through partnerships.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, the managing general partner (or its authorised representative) and each designated account signatory must attend an in-person identity interview at a Luxembourg branch or before a Luxembourg notary public for the initial account opening of an SCSp. The Luxembourg Law of 25 March 2020 permits remote identification via eIDAS-qualified electronic signatures and live video KYC at the bank's discretion; however, for an SCSp with non-resident limited partners, physical presence of the general partner is effectively mandatory, while silent limited partners may be onboarded remotely with notarised documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp absence of legal personality and tax-transparent status creating UBO traceability and substance questions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised partnership agreement and contribution deed; RCS registration extract; Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) confirmation of UBO disclosure; Luxembourg tax counsel opinion confirming tax transparency and the absence of anti-abuse exposure; general-partner treasury resolutions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multi-jurisdictional cross-border partner chain with potential politically exposed person (PEP) or sanctions exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified identity and address documents for all partners and UBOs; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds file (audited accounts, tax returns, bank references); group structure chart; negative PEP and sanctions screening results per partner; FATCA/CRS self-certifications; due-diligence questionnaires.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume e-commerce settlement flows from Stripe and PayPal lacking a conventional documentary trade trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform merchant agreements and verification certificates; structured settlement and transaction-export reports; chargeback and refund ledgers; commercial invoices with delivery tracking; ISAE 3402/SOC 2 reports of the payment processors; reconciled sales and inventory sub-ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound trade disbursements to musical-instrument manufacturers in currency-control or higher-risk jurisdictions (e.g., PRC, Vietnam, Indonesia).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Validated purchase orders, pro-forma invoices, and supplier contracts; Incoterms declarations, customs entries, and transport documents; supplier credit and sanctions checks; FX hedging confirmations; correspondent-bank KYC pack.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Early capital repatriation or partner-advance recharacterisation risk under ATAD and withholding-tax rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Partners' minute approving the distribution or withdrawal; updated capital-account statements; tax opinion confirming no deemed withholding tax on SCSp profit allocations; substance calendar (meeting minutes, office lease, bank mandate); advance tax ruling or CSSF confirmation where applicable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant route: (i) partner wires via SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA contributors or SEPA Credit Transfer for EEA contributors, referencing the SCSp's RCS register number and the relevant contribution clause of the partnership agreement; (ii) ISO 20022 Category Purpose codes — 'CALA' (Capital Increase) for equity-like injections, 'CASH' for treasury concentration, and 'COMC'/'TRAD' for merchant settlement from Stripe/PayPal; (iii) pre-wire verification bundle: general-partner treasury resolution, source-of-funds file per contributor, RBE extract, and BCL balance-of-payments statistical form when the transaction exceeds the direct-reporting threshold; (iv) funds are parked in a segregated capital-escrow/collection account pending KYC sign-off, then swept to the operational account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Luxembourg-prescribed clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for cross-border supplier invoices with Category Purpose code 'TRAD' or 'COMC' and structured remittance-info fields for automated reconciliation; (ii) SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for EEA/EU suppliers requiring T+0 settlement; (iii) documentary letters of credit (SWIFT MT700) or URC 522 documentary collections for bulk ex-works purchases from overseas manufacturers, with Incoterms and transport documents attached; (iv) all disbursements are cleared exclusively through the Luxembourg operating account to preserve the audit trail, and wire-level screening is run against EU/UN sanctions lists.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright vanilla EUR/USD forward contracts for supplier and inventory-cost hedging
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted or thinly traded currency pairs (e.g., USD/CNY via CNH) for exposure to Asian manufacturers
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD and EUR/CNY) for staggered capital-repayment and liquidity-margin management
Matched FX swap rollovers (tom-next/spot-forward) under a collateralised ISDA/CSA with the treasury bank, subject to EMIR NFC- threshold monitoring

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of RCS registration data (confirmation annuelle des donnees au Registre de Commerce et des Societes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / RCS Luxembourg via LBR eFile
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the anniversary of RCS registration; must also be performed at least once per calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late confirmation exposes the SCSp to administrative fines of up to EUR 250 (approx. USD 275) per offence; continued default after formal notice may lead to RCS strike-off and dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial owner confirmation declaration (confirmation annuelle au Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once per calendar year and no later than one month after the anniversary date of the RBE registration; updates for any ownership change must be made within 15 days.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm UBO data is punishable by criminal fines up to EUR 1,250 (approx. USD 1,375) and imprisonment of six months in serious cases, plus administrative fines for repeated non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts (depot des comptes annuels) and balance sheet
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS) via LBR eFile
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months of the financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, filing is due by 31 July or the next working day.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger court-ordered periodic penalty payments (astreintes) and fines up to EUR 5,000 (approx. USD 5,500); persistent non-filing can result in forced strike-off and liquidation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual municipal business tax and partnership income allocation declaration (declaration de l'impot commercial communal et declaration de repartition des resultats)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year entities, the declaration is due by 31 May (or the published extended date, generally 31 December for electronically filed returns).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing/omission exposes the SCSp and its general partner to late-payment interest at 0.6% per month, administrative fines of EUR 750-1,000, and estimated assessment by the ACD.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit by an approved independent auditor (reviseur d'entreprises) applies when the SCSp exceeds at least two of three thresholds: balance sheet total EUR 4.4m, net turnover EUR 8.8m, average workforce 50 employees; audit is also required if mandated by the partnership agreement, requested by partners, or imposed under applicable investment-fund or financial-sector legislation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the law of 19 December 2002 on undertakings, as amended; EU-adopted IFRS is permitted for voluntary use and is mandatory for the consolidated financial statements of listed undertakings.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The gérant must annually confirm all RBE beneficial-owner information within one month of registration anniversary and at least once each calendar year. Any transfer of partnership interests or change in ownership percentages must be filed with the RBE within 15 days of the transaction; the annual confirmation is then adjusted to reflect the updated shareholding structure.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200-3,500 per year for Luxembourg domiciliation and registered-office services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,500-16,500 per engagement when the statutory audit threshold is triggered; no mandatory audit below thresholds unless contractually or structurally required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate headline rate for Luxembourg City (2025): 17% corporate income tax (CIT), 1.19% solidarity surcharge (7% of CIT), and 6.75% municipal business tax (base rate 3% applied with municipal coefficient 2.25). A reduced 15% CIT rate applies to taxable income up to EUR 175,000, with a progressive 15% to 17% scale between EUR 175,001 and EUR 200,000.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: A Luxembourg SCSp is fiscally transparent by default (LIR Arts. 4, 5 and 185): no entity-level CIT, no municipal business tax on transparent income, and no net wealth tax at the SCSp level; each partner is taxed directly on its allocable profit share. A Luxembourg-resident corporate partner benefits from reduced 15% CIT on the first EUR 175,000; 80% IP-box exemption on qualifying musical/audio software IP (effective aggregate rate approximately 4.99%); 100% participation exemption on qualifying shareholdings; investment tax credits of 8% to 12%; and foreign tax credits for treaty-source income. For a non-resident partner without a Luxembourg permanent establishment, the effective Luxembourg tax rate on the online sales profit may be 0% at entity level, subject to the home-state taxation of the distributed profit.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite carryforward (no time limit) under LIR Art. 109; however, annual utilization is capped at 80% of positive taxable income for tax years from 2017 onward, with the cap temporarily suspended for certain relief years (including FY2023 and FY2024); losses carried forward must be claimed item by item in the tax return, and no carryback is available.
